Mandatory assistive guidance disclaimer and limitations

DrishtiAI provides AI-assisted environmental perception, navigation, and voice assistance. Detection and navigation may be affected by lighting, weather, camera limitations, sensor errors, connectivity, GPS accuracy, or environmental conditions.
Low light, direct sunlight glare, heavy rain, or fog can degrade camera object and hazard detection.
Urban canyons and covered structures can degrade GPS precision. Clock directions are advisory.
Computer vision models can produce false positives or miss fast-moving objects. Never rely solely on AI for street crossing.
Cloud services may be unavailable in low network areas. On-device vision continues locally.
External sensors are optional accessories. Ultrasonic and ToF readings can be affected by soft or angled surfaces.
Always use appropriate personal safety practices, a traditional white cane where recommended, and independent awareness when travelling.
This notice explains how DrishtiAI handles personal data and is designed with applicable Indian privacy requirements in mind.
Camera frames and microphone audio for obstacle detection and voice commands are processed 100% on your device. Camera video frames are never stored, transmitted, or uploaded to any server.
Right to Access: View profile data, linked guardians, and saved settings anytime.
Right to Correction: Update emergency contacts and preferences in Settings.
Right to Revoke: Immediately revoke any linked guardian connection with one tap.
Right to Erasure: Request permanent deletion of your account and related records.
DrishtiAI requires hardware permissions to provide assistive mobility. We practice data minimization: sensors are active only during your active sessions.
Used for real-time obstacle detection, hazard warnings, drop-off detection, and text recognition. Frames are processed in memory and never stored or uploaded.
Used for voice navigation commands and offline wake phrase detection. Audio is not recorded or stored remotely.
Used for pedestrian walking directions, nearby place discovery, and sharing emergency coordinates with your approved guardians during SOS.
Used optionally to connect to external smart cane accessories. Not required for core phone navigation.
Please read these Terms carefully before using DrishtiAI. By using this application, you acknowledge and agree to these terms.

DrishtiAI is an assistive technology aid. It does not replace personal judgment, traditional mobility training, or a standard white cane. The developers and contributors are not liable for navigation errors, accidents, or third-party service interruptions.
Emergency SOS alerts depend on cellular reception, battery levels, and guardian device availability. In immediate danger, call national emergency services (112) directly.
Guardian links require mutual agreement via pairing codes. You may revoke guardian access at any time through Settings.
SOS alerts your configured emergency contacts and approved guardians with your current GPS location.
SMS and network delivery depend on cellular signal, carrier availability, and battery level.
DrishtiAI is NOT a replacement for national emergency dispatch. Always call 112 directly in life-threatening situations.
DrishtiAI is built with defense-in-depth principles: Row Level Security (RLS) on all database tables, encrypted tokens in Android EncryptedSharedPreferences, and zero server storage of visual frames.
All queries are strictly partitioned by authenticated user UUID. Users cannot read or modify data belonging to other accounts.
Guardian pairing codes are 6-digit cryptographic tokens that expire in 15 minutes, with rate-limiting and brute-force protection.
Computer vision inference runs on-device using quantized TFLite models. No camera frames ever leave your device.
DrishtiAI combines on-device machine vision and offline speech interpretation. Because this system guides mobility in the physical world, its limitations must be transparently understood.
False Positives: Neural networks can misclassify floor patterns, shadows, or street grates as obstacles.
Missed Detections: Transparent glass doors, thin hanging wires, or fast-moving obstacles may occasionally be missed.
Lighting: Pitch darkness or severe glare degrades optical detection.
Voice: Heavy ambient traffic noise or regional dialects may require repeating commands.
